Mar 28, 1776: Paine encourages gunpowder manufacturing in Maryland; A prisoner escape is foiled; Troops & Militia continue the march to New York; Pirates infest the coast, & more!
Mar 27, 1776: Franklin Slogs North; Goods Sail to France; Boyd's Late With Muskets, Jay Smells A Rat; Wolcott Wonders Where the British Will Attack Next , & more!
Mar 26, 1776: Gerry: "Americans Kicked British Butt In Boston"; Patriot Gov. Ward Dead By Smallpox; Guns Scarce Everywhere; Gunpowder Scarce Everywhere; Mr. Winey Sold Guns That Need Fixin', & more!
Mar 25, 1776: BOSTON IS LIBERATED! BRITISH WITHDRAW LEAVING FAMISHED HORSES BEHIND! Young's son gets a break, Hancock's property is tended to, is Canada really a separate Department, and more!
Mar 24, 1776: USS Lexington preps for defending the coast, there's a flour shipment mixup, Patriots win a fight in North Carolina, Whipple's got info for raising and curing hemp, and more!

Mar 23, 1776: New Privateering Act hits the Colonies, Adams ponders Colony Unity, Gold and Silver Sent to Canada, Flag with Rattle Snake and "Don't Tread On Me" spotted, and more!

Mar 22, 1776: Maryland tables privateering preamble debates, Capt. Shippen authorized to cruise Chesapeak Bay, Minute Men ask for money, Franklin heads north to Canada with ideas of a Union, and more!
Mar 21, 1776: Americans encouraged to grow Flax, Hemp, Cotton, & Wool. John Jay worries about safety with British sympathizers around. Congress debates if unarmed Men should be disbanded, and more!
Common Sense; Addressed to the Inhabitants of America
Mar 20, 1776: "Whether we be reconciled to Great Britain, or separated from her perhaps forever is a question which a few weeks may probably decide..." Letters from Duane, Hewes, Lewis and more!
Mar 19, 1776: John Adams drafts "Thoughts On Government" which includes term limits! Copies of Common Sense are everywhere, Maryland pleads for cannons, Sam Adams visits a new Tavern, and more!
Mar 18, 1776: Richard Smith recounts Continental Congress happenings, including votes for Letters of Marque and Privateering British (but not Irish) property
Mar 17, 1776: John Adams pens his wife, Allen is suspicious of Connecticut, NY prepares for war, France gets Sweden to prevent Russia from coming to Britain's aid, and more!
Mar 16, 1776: Hancock moves gunpowder supplies to New York. Intercepted letters bring valuable intelligence from overseas including France is inclined to support the American cause! Plus much more!
Mar 15, 1776: NY Prepares For War! Hancock: "I Trust by the Blessings of God, our United & Spirited exertions will baffle the Designs of our Enemies, secure & preserve the Liberties of our Country"
Mar 14, 1776: President Hancock orders 8,000 troops to New York. Secret Committee purchases swords, arms & ammunition. Livingston proposes a Day of Fasting and Prayer, & Prescott issues a complaint

Mar 13, 1776: Hooper pens Trumbull: Congrats on holding Dorchester Heights! Also, Lord Cornwallis tries to divide American unity. Congress debates using privateers to help fight the British, and more!
Mar 12, 1776: North Carolina's William Hooper warns of the British attempts at dividing the United Colonies: "Heaven Grant that America may have virtues to resist their lures"
The 1776 Continental Dollar: Mind Your Business
Mar 11, 1776: Franklin & group are headed to Canada. Hancock writes to Washington about recent promotions. Smith recounts activities in the Continental Congress, & Samuel Ward pens his captured son
Mar 10, 1776: Morris pens Silas Deane - Better head off to France ASAP before the seas are crawling with Men of War and Privateers
Mar 9, 1776: BRITISH MAN of WAR IN BALTIMORE HARBOR! Gunpowder shipments rushed in! Wolcott: If every American was well furnished with the Means of Defense, we'd be a Match for the World
Mar 8, 1776: John Adams suspects the British will attack from the north. Continental Congress forms Comm. to Encourage Manufacture of Firearms, Wolcott is amazed by Rittenhouse's Orrery, and more!
Mar 7, 1776: John Hancock is anxious about shipbuilding, wants to fight for his Colony. Thomas and Schuyler head north to Canada, & Melchoir gets pissy when a promotion doesn't meet his expectations
Mar 6, 1776: The United American Colonies prep for a summer of WAR: "America never can support her freedom til we have a sufficient source of arms and ammunition of all species among ourselves.."
Mar 5, 1776: Bartlett has some harsh words for his Colony, although their spirit in raising a regiment for Canada is noted. Lord Drummond stirs up controversy with some unauthorized discussions.
Mar 4, 1776: Joseph Hewes discusses supplies sent to No. Carolina, John Jay pens personal matters to a friend, Sam Ward updates brother on American fortifications, & everyone hates the roads.
Mar 3, 1776: William Whipple pens his brother: Genl Lee fortifying N. York, stops comms from mainland to British Men of War. John Adams gets philosophical, and wonders about France
Mar 2, 1776: Bartlett is pissed at the British. Secret Committee sends spy to France: Will you support American independence? Whipple airs come complaints & Oliver Wolcott pens a letter to his wife.
March 1, 1776: John Adams "A martial Spirit has Seized all the Colonies". Secret Comm approves $$ for necessary goods. W. Alexander promoted for his Zeal and attachment to the American cause, & more!
Feb. 28, 1776: John Hancock advises Gen. Charles Lee stay his journey to Canada, Richard Smith offers more details of committee work, a frenchman brings half a ton of gunpowder

Feb. 27, 1776: Robert Alexander of Maryland reports smuggled copy of Britain's Conciliatory Act confirms American vessels to be seized! Congress requests update from Baltimore. More from Smith's diary
Feb. 26, 1776: Sam Adams longs for home, Bartlett wants gun powder to fight off the British in the spring, Ben Franklin submits a motion for trade, the Secret Committee meets, and Smith's diary
February 25, 1776: NY colonist James Duane updates the NY Provincial Convention, 4 Battalions are raised in NY for defence. John Jay writes to Robert Livingston, and Mr. Ross requests a passport
On this day, February 24, 1776, NY colonist James Duane defends a friend, discusses frigates to the Marine Committee, laments his distance from home and worries about contractors.
